title: Structured enterprise intake and prioritization rubric for hosted API chat/streaming/tool-calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a pragmatic, repeatable intake pipeline and decision rubric for enterprise-hosted API feature requests specifically targeting chat, streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured outputs. The rubric should help prioritize requests by customer value, compliance/risk, engineering cost, and alignment with Redwood’s serving and reliability thesis.

Scope:
- Define intake form fields and required artifacts for frontline CS/AMs to submit (customer goal, scale, privacy/regulatory constraints, example prompts, required latency/throughput SLOs, output structure/schema).
- Build a lightweight scoring rubric (quantitative) with clear thresholds for auto-prioritization vs. escalation to product council.
- Create routing rules for requests: self-serve backlog, PM triage, Eng/Design discovery, or enterprise roadmap.
- Produce templates for follow-up questions and standardized cost/effort estimates (engineering, infra, QA).
- Define acceptance criteria for requests that can be delivered as hosted API features vs. require Dedicated/Private deployment or custom engineering.

Out of scope: full automation into billing or Dedicated procurement flow (follow-up work). Deep technical design of runtime changes is owned by Eng.

Why now: Increasing volume of enterprise asks with partial/ambiguous requirements is causing long lead times and misaligned expectations. Teams need a fast, repeatable way to determine which requests are high ROI for hosted API improvements (vs. sales-assisted Dedicated/Private work).

Success metrics:
- Time to initial triage decision reduced from median 10 business days to <= 3 business days.
- >60% of intake submissions have sufficient artifacts to get an initial estimate without follow-up.
- Decrease in misroutes (requests routed to hosted that clearly require Private/Dedicated) by 75% in first quarter post-launch.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form (Confluence + Intake form prototype) published and adopted by CS (pilot with 3 AMs).
- Scoring rubric documented with numeric weights and example scored requests.
- Routing automation rules drafted and implemented as a checklist in Linear + a Notion/Confluence workflow.
- Playbook for PM/Eng/Design discovery follows the rubric and includes a template of required tests (latency/cost/quality checks).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Overly prescriptive intake may slow down sales; mitigate with a fast-path minimal form for urgent enterprise deals.
- Numeric rubric may not capture nuanced brand/customer relationships; include an override path requiring documented rationale.
- Some high-value requests will still require deep Eng design and may not be deliverable in-hosted; ensure clear messaging to sales on expected outcomes.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Aisha Patel (owner), Diego Martinez (assignee for rollout), Rajiv Kapoor (PM partner).
- Eng: Priya Singh (runtime), Marc Liu (infra).
- Sales/CS: Elise Gómez (CS lead), Tomas Novak (AM pilot).
- Design: Lina Chen (console/UX for intake).

Next steps:
1) Build initial intake form prototype and share with CS pilot (by 2026-03-05).
2) Draft numeric rubric and test with 10 historical enterprise requests (by 2026-03-12).
3) Iterate rubric based on pilot feedback; finalize routing rules and training material (by 2026-03-24).
4) Rollout to CS and Sales with a 4-week feedback loop (releases: console-2026.04 for intake UX).
